evidence: tests/unit/test_ci_provider_matrix.py:238 builds `cfg = LLMConfig.from_env(repo_root=project)` through the REAL layering but then asserts only `cfg.max_iterations == 7` (line 239) and `cfg.timeout_s == 123` (line 243) — it never asserts `cfg.model`, the exact surface the leak lived on.

src/rebar/llm/config.py:575: `model=_llm_str(table, cli, "REBAR_LLM_MODEL", "model", DEFAULT_MODEL)` where `table` comes from `_read_llm_file_table` -> `layer_llm_config_file` (config.py:340-351), i.e. the `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` overlay path this test already exercises.

The layered-`cfg.model` behavioral assertion exists ONLY in tests/external/test_provider_matrix_live.py:70-77 (`LLMConfig.from_env().model`), gated by `@_live_llm.skip_without_live_llm`/`@_skip_unless_ci_arm` — skipped everywhere except a credentialed CI arm, and the LLM lane runs weekly on real money (per the module docstring, tests/unit/test_ci_provider_matrix.py:4-6).

The static test `test_each_overlay_sets_only_the_model_selection_keys` (line 151-176) reads raw TOML with `tomllib.loads(...read_text())`; it catches a missing/mis-qualified key in the file but not a regression in how that key layers into `cfg.model`.
